intro: Looking for a couples counsellor near you usually means something in your relationship feels stuck, painful or hard to talk about alone. You may want someone local you can see face to face, or you may simply want a counsellor who understands the particular strain you and your partner are under. We can introduce you to a UK counsellor who works with couples, and they will discuss their approach and quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a couples counsellor near them often need
need_lead: Most people who search for a couples counsellor near me are looking for practical, local help with a relationship that has become difficult.
needs: You and your partner keep having the same argument and cannot find a way through it on your own.
One of you has suggested counselling and the other is unsure, so you need someone who can help you both feel comfortable.
You want to talk about intimacy, trust or a change in your relationship with a counsellor who is trained in relationship therapy.
You would prefer to see someone in person near where you live, rather than only online.
You are separating or considering separation and want help to communicate more clearly about what happens next.
context_heading: What to know about finding a couples counsellor near you
context: In the UK, the titles counsellor and psychotherapist are not protected by law, so anyone can use them. To protect yourself, look for a practitioner on a register accredited by the Professional Standards Authority, such as BACP, UKCP or NCPS. Accredited registers require training, supervision, a code of ethics and a complaints procedure.

A good therapist will explain their approach, confidentiality and its limits in the first session. When you search for a couples counsellor near me, it is worth asking whether they work specifically with couples and whether they offer online sessions as well as in-person ones, so you can choose what suits you both.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say that you are looking for a couples counsellor and whether you want sessions in person near you or online.
Mention the main issue you want help with, such as conflict, intimacy or a change in your relationship.
Let us know if you and your partner have different ideas about starting counselling, so the counsellor can take that into account.
Tell us your general location so we can introduce you to a counsellor who works in your area or online.
Say whether you have seen a counsellor before and whether you have a preference for a particular approach.
Include any practical needs, such as accessibility requirements or preferred session times, so the counsellor can respond usefully.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the couples counsellor
questions: What training have you had in relationship therapy and couples counselling?
Are you on a register accredited by the Professional Standards Authority, and if so, which one?
Do you offer online sessions as well as in-person sessions near me?
How do you usually work with couples, and what happens in the first session?
What are your confidentiality arrangements and its limits when working with a couple?
How do you help couples discuss their goals together at the start?

faqs.q: Do we both need to attend every session?
faqs.a: Couples counsellors usually work with both partners together, but some also offer individual sessions alongside. It is worth asking the counsellor how they structure sessions when you first make contact.

faqs.q: How do we choose a couples counsellor near us?
faqs.a: Look for someone with relationship-specific training and check whether they are on a register accredited by the Professional Standards Authority, such as BACP, UKCP or NCPS. A first conversation can help you see whether you both feel comfortable with their approach.

faqs.q: Can we have couples counselling online if we cannot find someone nearby?
faqs.a: Many counsellors offer online sessions as well as in-person work, so it is worth asking. Online counselling can be useful if one of you travels or if local availability is limited.

faqs.q: What if my partner is reluctant to come?
faqs.a: It is common for one partner to be more hesitant, and a counsellor can discuss this with you. You can ask whether they offer an initial conversation to help your partner understand what is involved.
